adoption.notes: The runtime signs the unchanged command bytes and never reissues a command: egress publishes once, held by tests on its call sites, its scheduling and its client. It reads rate_limited only as a firmware-telemetry/v2 fault. It drives no firmware-commanded zone, so the Tier D attempt carve-out has no runtime path yet. No conformance claim is made, so the version is not frozen by this merge. It publishes liveness at v 1 only: it generates no nonce and keeps no liveness table. It signs commands and liveness over the object bytes alone, not yet in the domains of Signing Domains, and reads no runtime_key_domains; its liveness signer, which signs that way, ships in v2.5.0, so no released runtime signs in the domains.

Its device verifier implements runtime liveness at v 1, which firmware-commands/v1's baseline audit moved to this version's Runtime Liveness section, and records whether the runtime is reachable as shadow observability. It signs the rate_limited verdict at fault v 2 from a3c54c2, and does not yet accept liveness at v 2. No conformance claim is made. Its verifiers check commands and liveness over the object bytes alone, not yet in the domains of Signing Domains.

notes: Exists for the rate_limited verdict, which answers relay_close only, and for the rule that a runtime never reissues a command to recover its delivery. Fresh open_protected_circuit attempts for a latched Tier D trip are not reissues and continue, under the binding the governing safety-profile contract authorizes. Command and provisioning approval bytes are v1's and keep v 1. Runtime liveness at v 1 keeps the grammar of this version's Runtime Liveness section and gains v 2, carrying a fresh 128-bit nonce from which the signing runtime bounds how long ago a device began the transaction behind a reading, under firmware-telemetry/v2; nothing implements liveness v 2 yet. Runtime liveness at v 1 is implemented by the runtime signer and the edge firmware verifier, which is implementation and not end-to-end or HIL proof; no device image gates a Local Interlock on it. The runtime has adopted the rate_limited and no-reissue rules; the edge firmware signs the rate_limited verdict from a3c54c2. The runtime adopts it before any device signs a v 2 fault, and devices accept liveness v 2 before the runtime publishes it. The runtime command key signs a command and a liveness message only in the domain of its purpose, under Signing Domains, keeps no v 1 form, and signs for a device only while its manifest declares runtime_key_domains under firmware-telemetry/v2. Neither implementation signs, verifies or declares in those domains yet; the runtime adopts first.
